controls.name: mutant-is-live
controls.must_fire_because: a 0/64 from a dead mutant, a failed rebuild or a missed anchor is indistinguishable from a 0/64 the corpus genuinely did not notice
controls.can_fail_because: a feature-gated or semantically inert edit leaves probe_base == probe_mut and the mutation is reported VOID with no rate
controls.null_must_contain: the probe output BEFORE and AFTER each mutation, which must differ
controls.detail: every mutation changed its own probe, so every rate below is about the corpus

controls.name: two-fault-classes-are-inexpressible
controls.must_fire_because: the row's finding: the corpus executes `<` and cannot observe its fault
controls.can_fail_because: a corpus program that compares equal values would make less-is-lesseq non-zero
controls.null_must_contain: a per-mutation detection count, which must be capable of being non-zero -- three of the five are
controls.detail: less-is-lesseq 0/64 and stdlib-init 0/64 while sub-is-add, resolver-message and stdlib-if are non-zero

controls.name: classes-are-not-uniform
controls.must_fire_because: if every mutation scored the same the corpus classes would be interchangeable and the by_class split would carry no information
controls.can_fail_because: five identical totals would mean the sweep is not discriminating between mutations at all
controls.null_must_contain: the five totals, which must not all be equal
controls.detail: totals 4, 0, 24, 5, 0 -- four distinct values across five mutations

falsifier: if a fresh sweep gave different rates, or any probe failed to move, the recorded rates are about this harness and not about the corpus
